findings.finding: phase.locator("> div").nth(1)` relies on the phase row's second direct child being the description. If the row's child structure ever changes (a wrapper, an icon div), the test silently measures the wrong element's `color` — and since all siblings inherit the same color from the container, it would still pass or fail misleadingly. A `getByText`/role-based locator (or asserting the element's class/text) would be more robust.
findings.suggestion: Locate the description via a stable attribute (e.g. a class or the text content) instead of positional child index, or add an assertion on the element's content before measuring.

findings.finding: The RGB parser accepts `rgba(...)` but ignores the alpha channel. If the container background ever becomes translucent (or Chromium returns e.g. `color(srgb ...)` / `oklch(...)` under a different color space setting), the math is wrong or the helper throws — the throw is fine (fails loudly), but translucent backgrounds would be computed against black.
findings.suggestion: Reject alpha < 1 explicitly, or fall back to a screenshot-based/`element.scrollWidth`-independent check. Low priority since the container background is opaque today.
